title: Positive Advantage Implies Bounded-Space Recognition
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $L$ be a language of bit strings, and let $s:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, $c\in\mathbb{N}$, and $\delta\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\delta$. Suppose that on every input $x$, every choice string of some length $T$ leads $N$ to halt, and the probability that its output equals the Boolean indicator of membership of $x$ in $L$ is at least $1/2+\delta$. Suppose also that on every input and every choice string, the total number of distinct work-tape cells visited is at most $c s(|x|)$. Then $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{BPSPACE}(s)$, meaning that some finite nondeterministic Turing machine uses at most a constant multiple of $s(|x|)$ space, halts on every branch within an input-dependent finite time, and outputs the correct membership indicator with probability at least $2/3$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
$L$ is a language of bit strings
$s$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
For each input there is a time bound $T$ by which all branches halt
Output equals the membership indicator with probability at least $1/2+\delta$
Space on every input and choice string is at most $c s(|x|)$
